cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church in Corinth, and he's just finished a whole chapter on love. Now he keeps rolling. Earnestly pursue love, he says, and eagerly desire spiritual gifts.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians to eagerly desire spiritual gifts. Which gift does he single out?

cards.text: First up is speaking in a tongue. Paul says that person speaks to God, not to men, and no one understands him, so I bet the rest of the room is just nodding politely.

cards.question: Someone speaking in a tongue speaks to God, and no one understands him. Paul says the one who prophesies speaks to people.

cards.text: YES. Prophecy speaks to people for their edification, encouragement and comfort, and friend, that's not a gift, that's a whole care package.

cards.question: Paul says the one who speaks in a tongue builds up the whole church.
The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the ___.

cards.text: Now hold on, Paul's not tossing tongues out of the kitchen. He says he wishes ALL of them could speak in tongues, but he'd rather have them prophesy.

cards.question: Paul says the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, with one exception. What is it?

answers.text: Unless the whole church joins in

cards.text: Then Paul makes it personal: if he came to them speaking in tongues, how would that help them, unless he brought some revelation, knowledge, prophecy or teaching? Friend, if I showed up in your kitchen speaking only Stamper, you'd smile, nod, and QUIETLY go look up a recipe.

So Paul pulls out some everyday examples, starting with lifeless instruments like the flute and the harp. I spent YEARS as a lifeless tool in a junk drawer, friend, so I'm taking that word personally.

cards.question: Paul says a flute or a harp needs distinct notes so anyone can recognize the tune.
Paul's next example is a trumpet. If it sounds a muffled call, what happens?

answers.text: No one gets ready for battle

cards.question: A blurry flute and a muffled trumpet. What's Paul's point for the Corinthians?

answers.text: Their words must be understood to help

cards.text: Paul says there are many different languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning. Even the noises my oven makes mean SOMETHING, friend, I just haven't cracked the code yet.

cards.question: Paul says if he doesn't know the meaning of someone's language, he is a ___ to the speaker, and the speaker is one to him.
The Corinthians are eager to have spiritual gifts. Which gifts does Paul tell them to strive to excel in?

answers.text: The gifts that build up the church
The gifts that are hardest to get

cards.question: Paul says the one who speaks in a tongue should pray for something. What is it?

answers.text: That he may speak more often

cards.text: Here's why. Paul says when he prays in a tongue, his spirit is praying.

cards.question: When Paul prays in a tongue, his spirit prays, but his mind is ___.

cards.text: So what's Paul's plan? He'll pray with his spirit AND pray with his mind, the full team, nobody sitting on the bench.

cards.question: When it comes to singing, Paul says he'll sing with his spirit and leave his mind out of it.

cards.text: Now picture someone uninstructed sitting in the room while you speak a blessing in spirit and give thanks.

cards.question: Someone speaks a blessing in spirit. How can the uninstructed person say ___ to it, when he doesn't know what was said?

cards.text: Paul says you may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person isn't built up. It's like getting added to a group text where everybody's saying THANK YOU SO MUCH, and you heart it anyway with NO idea what for.

cards.question: Paul has been putting prophecy ahead of tongues, but he also says he speaks in tongues more than all of the Corinthians.
Even so, in the church, what would Paul rather speak than ten thousand words in a tongue?

answers.text: Five clear words that instruct others

cards.text: FIVE words beat TEN THOUSAND, friend, and that's every work meeting that should've been an email. Then Paul says it straight: “Brothers, stop thinking like children.”

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians to stop thinking like children. But in what area does he say to be like infants?

cards.text: In your thinking, though, be mature. Then Paul quotes the Law: “By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”

cards.question: After that quote, Paul says tongues are a sign for believers, not for unbelievers.

cards.text: Right: tongues are a sign for unbelievers, and prophecy is for believers. Now Paul paints a picture where the whole church comes together, everyone speaks in tongues, and in walk some uninstructed people or unbelievers.

cards.question: The whole church is speaking in tongues when visitors walk in. What does Paul say they'll say?

answers.text: That you are out of your minds
That you are just showing off
That you are a holy people

cards.text: But flip it: everyone's prophesying, and an unbeliever or uninstructed person walks in. He's convicted and called to account by all, and the secrets of his heart are made known.

cards.question: The visitor is convicted and the secrets of his heart are made known. What does he do?

answers.text: He falls facedown and worships God
He walks out without saying a word
He asks someone to interpret for him

cards.text: And he proclaims it: “God is truly among you!” That's where we'll set the dough down for now, friend, because Paul is NOT done teaching this church yet.
